Let \(X_{k}\) denote \(2^{k}\) except with leading zeroes added to make it four digits long. Let \(\overline{a b c \cdots}\) denote the number obtained upon concatenating \(a, b, c, \ldots\) We have

\[2^{6} \cdot \overline{X_{0} X_{1} \ldots X_{5}}=\overline{X_{6} X_{7} \ldots X_{11}}\]

Therefore, \(\overline{X_{0} X_{1} \ldots X_{5}}\) divides \(\overline{X_{0} X_{1} \ldots X_{11}}\), meaning the remainder when \(\overline{X_{0} X_{1} \ldots X_{13}}\) is divided by \(\overline{X_{0} X_{1} \ldots X_{5}}\) is

\[\overline{X_{12} X_{13}}=40968192\]
